html:
A senior man of the Wangal clan of the Eora people of Port Jackson, who became the main go-between with the first British colony at Sydney. He was the first Aboriginal Australian to travel to Europe and return.

In November 1789, Governor Arthur Phillip had Bennelong captured, hoping to learn the language and customs of the local people. The colony had arrived with the First Fleet the year before, and a smallpox epidemic had just killed many of the Eora. Bennelong escaped in May 1790. A few months later Phillip was speared at Manly at a gathering Bennelong attended, but soon after Bennelong began to visit the settlement on his own terms. Phillip built him a hut on the point now called Bennelong Point, where the Sydney Opera House stands.

In 1792 he sailed to England with Phillip, together with a younger man, Yemmerrawanne, who died there. Bennelong returned in 1795. He lived on with his people around the harbour until his death in 1813. He stands at the start of the long story of contact between the colony and Aboriginal Australians.
